newsitem.title: UK: Hiscox wins syndicate merger approval.
newsitem.headline: Hiscox wins syndicate merger approval.

text.p: Lloyd's of London insurance group, Hiscox Plc on Wednesday said it had received overwhelming support for plans to merge its syndicates into one fully integrated entity with capacity of 360 million pounds ($587.2 million).
The company's chairman Robert Hiscox also said that it was planning to join the full stock exchange in July, helping to widen investment in the group by institutions.
Hiscox is currently listed on the the alternative investment market (AIM).
The company's results will be released next week.
Over 98 percent of syndicate members who voted supported the proposals to merge syndicates 33, 52 and 625 at an extraordinary meeting on Tuesday.
The merged syndicate will trade from the 1998 year of account. In 1997 the syndicate would have been the second largest trading in the Lloyd's insurance market.

"We are delighted with the endorsement of the merger by members of the syndicates. Our Lloyd's business will now be one cohesive fighting machine which will strive to be the best with renewed vigour," said chairman Robert Hiscox.
Hiscox believes the move will lead to increased returns and reduced costs to members.

It also gives the syndicate more flexibility to underwrite bigger lines within its chosen areas of business and attract "Running three businesses with separate capital bases and keeping underwriting separate is relatively complicated and expensive and there will be savings," said Hiscox.
However, the main driver was the attraction of being a composite syndicate, he said.
"Being able to offer marine and non-marine insurance to one client and the full array of talents in one policy from contract frustration, political risk, cargo or confiscation is much better for us."

But he said that no decision had been made on whether to buy out Names -- the traditional backers of the market -- after the group applied to the market's ruling council for permission to do so earlier this year.
Hiscox said the move was a precaution made to keep its options open.
There were savings to be made and advantages to having one source of capital supplying both its Lloyd's business and its insurance company.
But in order to replace the Names capacity the company would have to put up around 150 million pounds and he said the company recognised the advantages of the current situation.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721 ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
